metadata.description: Layer 2 Forward-Durability Framework: five indicator data, source-tagged
metadata.data_note: Data are pinned to the locked mid-2026 case-study dataset. API-backed sources are flagged refreshable for future updates; this version does not auto-refresh, to stay consistent with the report.

valuation.name: Valuation
valuation.score_summary: India's P/E premium to EM ex-India is ~24%, placing it in the caution band. The premium is real but not at a historical extreme, so the gate does not trip severe. Caps confidence; does not break the thesis.

data_points.label: India P/E premium to EM ex-India (w=12%)
India P/E premium to EM ex-India (w=13%)
data_points.source: Derived: (EM_PE - w*India_PE)/(1-w), then India_PE/EM_ex_PE - 1, with w=0.13

data_points.label: India P/E premium to EM ex-India (w=15%)
data_points.source: Derived: (EM_PE - w*India_PE)/(1-w), then India_PE/EM_ex_PE - 1, with w=0.15

data_points.label: Raw India P/E premium to uncorrected MSCI EM

historical_context.summary: Multiple credible sources report India's premium compressed below its 10-year average as of late 2025 to early 2026. Exact historical averages are behind Bloomberg/FactSet; direction only.

sources.label: Goldman via Reuters (Nov 10 2025)
sources.description: India's valuation premium to EM described as sharply lower vs Sept 2024, and defensible.

sources.label: Goldman via Reuters (Dec 31 2025)
sources.description: India's premium to global/EM had dipped below its 10-year average after 2025 underperformance.

sources.label: Reuters (Jul 1 2026)
sources.description: India's premium seen as more attractive after underperformance, though valuations remained relatively full.

valuation.acknowledged_limitation: Because the earnings-growth premium versus EM ex-India is not directly measured, the framework cannot fully determine whether India's valuation premium is justified. This is the main unresolved link between structural opportunity and future equity returns.

demographics.name: Demographics
demographics.score_summary: India's age structure is a genuine, durable, decade-plus advantage. Old-age dependency is less than half China's. The dividend is only partially realized (female LFP at 35%), which is both a shortfall and remaining upside.
demographics.conversion_caveat: A demographic dividend requires conversion into employment. Female LFP at 35% means the dividend is only partially realized, which is both a current shortfall and remaining upside if participation rises.

governance.name: Governance
governance.score_summary: India's governance profile is mixed against China and against a zero baseline. Clear advantage on Voice and Accountability has compressed and turned negative by 2023. China leads on Government Effectiveness and Control of Corruption. India better on Rule of Law, but both are in negative territory.

dimensions.name: Political Stability and Abs. of Violence

digital_adoption.name: Digital Financial Adoption
digital_adoption.score_summary: India lags the EM peer median by 23-33pp on digital payment adoption. Adoption is rising fast and consistently from a low base: any-digital-payment went from 22% (2014) to 48% (2024). A convergence-from-behind story, not established leadership.
digital_adoption.honest_note: This indicator was added to test the thesis's digital infrastructure bull pillar. The data partially disconfirms it: India's digital story is real but not a competitive advantage vs EM peers yet.

external_macro.name: External Macro Vulnerability
external_macro.score_summary: Real external vulnerability, but the persistent piece (currency drag) is mild and survivable. The severe piece (oil shock) is conditional, not structural. Caps confidence at the margin.
external_macro.note: Currency drag and oil exposure are scored as one indicator because oil shocks and rupee depreciation are largely the same underlying macro risk. Scoring them separately would double-count one vulnerability.

ladder_verdict.label: Structurally attractive, but priced and macro-sensitive
ladder_verdict.derivation: Neither gate tripped severe (valuation neutral-to-caution; external macro at-risk mild-conditional). The structural case is one strong pillar (demographics) plus two neutrals (governance lean-negative, digital adoption neutral). Per the pre-declared ladder rule: no severe gate plus incomplete structural support leads to Rung 3, not Rung 2.
ladder_verdict.verdict_statement: India's opportunity is real, especially through demographics, but the broader structural case is less decisive than the original bull narrative suggested. Governance is mixed, digital adoption is improving but not yet EM-leading, valuation still embeds a meaningful premium, and external macro risks remain live. The thesis is not broken (no gate trips severe), but future outperformance is conditional on earnings growth continuing to justify the premium.
ladder_verdict.thesis_answer: India's opportunity is real, but narrower than the original bull case implied. The market has partially priced in that opportunity through a meaningful valuation premium, though not to an obvious bubble or extreme level. The forward case is therefore conditionally durable: India can keep outperforming if earnings growth validates the premium, but the margin for disappointment is limited.
ladder_verdict.analysts_journey: Started India-skeptic / China-bull. Layer 1 disproved the historical skepticism (India clearly outperformed). Layer 2 vindicates the forward caution (real but priced, conditionally durable). The disproven hypothesis and the final verdict are consistent: the skepticism was wrong about the past, right to persist about the price going forward.
